system:
You are an art-world editor compiling a gallery guide for San Francisco, United States. Answer with the
JSON object the schema describes and nothing else. Rank by significance and influence in the
contemporary art world: programme quality, the artists represented, art-fair presence, critical and
institutional attention, and longevity. Include commercial galleries and the nonprofit, artist-run and
project spaces that show contemporary art to the public in San Francisco itself (galleries whose home is
elsewhere count only through a permanent San Francisco space). Exclude museums, art fairs, auction houses,
framers, art schools, decor shops, online-only dealers and advisories. For every gallery give its usual
name; its official website when you are confident of it, else null; the district it is in, using one of
these labels when it fits (Dogpatch/Minnesota Street, Potrero/SoMa, Union Square/Downtown, Mission, Chinatown/North Beach, Oakland/Berkeley) else the district name you know; a street address hint when you
know it (street and number are enough), else null; its kind (gallery, museum, nonprofit, project_space, university, other); and a short note on why it
matters. Every entry must be a distinct venue — list a gallery with several San Francisco spaces once.
user: What are the 100 most significant and influential galleries in San Francisco, ranked in order? If less than 100 significant galleries exist, provide the complete list of significant galleries.

galleries.name: Fraenkel Gallery
galleries.note: Founded 1979; the West Coast's most internationally significant photography-centred gallery, with Diane Arbus, Sophie Calle, Lee Friedlander, Richard Learoyd and Elisheva Biernoff, and a constant art-fair and museum presence.

galleries.name: Jessica Silverman
galleries.note: The city's most ambitious younger blue-chip dealer; Woody De Othello, Rupy C. Tut, Judy Chicago, Clare Rojas and Hayal Pozanti, with placements in major museum collections and top-tier fairs.

galleries.name: Gagosian San Francisco
galleries.note: The only mega-gallery with a permanent San Francisco outpost (opened 2016), bringing blue-chip international programming to the Bay Area.

galleries.name: Berggruen Gallery
galleries.note: John Berggruen's gallery, since 1970 the city's leading dealer in postwar and modern masters alongside a strong contemporary roster; purpose-built Hawthorne Street space.

galleries.name: Altman Siegel
galleries.note: Critically the sharpest contemporary programme in the city — Trevor Paglen, K.r.m. Mooney, Liam Everett, Shannon Ebner — with consistent biennial and museum crossover.

galleries.name: Crown Point Press
galleries.note: Kathan Brown's etching workshop and gallery since 1962; editions with Diebenkorn, Kentridge, Marioni, Julie Mehretu and Tomma Abts make it a historic engine of Bay Area art.

galleries.name: Haines Gallery
galleries.note: Founded 1987; Andy Goldsworthy, Zhan Wang, Ai Weiwei projects and leading Bay Area artists, now anchoring Minnesota Street Project after decades at 49 Geary.

galleries.name: CCA Wattis Institute for Contemporary Arts
galleries.note: The Bay Area's most intellectually influential kunsthalle-style exhibition and research space, with a curatorial fellowship pipeline and internationally followed programme.

galleries.name: Anglim/Trimble
galleries.note: Successor to Gallery Paule Anglim (est. 1970s), the keeper of Bay Area conceptual and Funk legacies: Deborah Oropallo, William T. Wiley, Tony Labat, Nathaniel Dorsky estate artists.

galleries.name: Catharine Clark Gallery
galleries.note: Since 1991 a pioneer of new-media and politically engaged art, with the Media Room video programme and artists such as Masami Teraoka, Sandow Birk and Stephanie Syjuco.

galleries.name: Hosfelt Gallery
galleries.note: Large warehouse space with a rigorous international programme — Jim Campbell, Emil Lukas, Liliana Porter, Alan Rath estate — and long fair participation.

galleries.name: Gallery Wendi Norris
galleries.note: Scholarly programme around Leonora Carrington, Remedios Varo and contemporary artists including Chitra Ganesh and María Magdalena Campos-Pons; pioneered a roving 'offsite' exhibition model.

galleries.name: Rena Bransten Gallery
galleries.note: Operating since 1974, a Bay Area institution showing Robert Colescott, Hung Liu, Rigo 23 and self-taught artists alongside emerging talent.

galleries.name: KADIST San Francisco
galleries.note: Collection-based international nonprofit with residencies, commissions and a globally networked exhibition and video programme.

galleries.name: Southern Exposure
galleries.note: Since 1974 the city's key artist-centred nonprofit: juried and curated exhibitions, Alternative Exposure grants and generations of Bay Area artists' first shows.

galleries.name: Institute of Contemporary Art San Francisco
galleries.note: Free, non-collecting kunsthalle opened 2022 that has quickly become a major platform for local and international contemporary artists.

galleries.name: Jenkins Johnson Gallery
galleries.note: Founded 1996; a leading champion of Black artists and photography — Gordon Parks, Ming Smith, Lava Thomas — with a Brooklyn project space and strong fair presence.

galleries.name: Casemore Gallery
galleries.note: Photography-forward programme (formerly Casemore Kirkeby) with artists such as Klea McKenna, Lucas Blalock and John Chiara; a critical hub for lens-based work.

galleries.name: Et al.
galleries.note: Beloved basement gallery under a Chinatown shop; scrappy, curatorially adventurous and disproportionately influential on the city's younger scene.

galleries.name: Ratio 3
galleries.note: Chris Perez's gallery has shaped two decades of Bay Area contemporary practice, showing Ruth Laskey, Mitzi Pederson, Takeshi Murata and Jordan Kantor.

galleries.name: Micki Meng
galleries.note: Grown out of Friends Indeed; a nimble, internationally connected dealer with New York collaborations and a sharply curated emerging roster.

galleries.name: Ever Gold [Projects]
galleries.note: Andrew McClintock's gallery pairs Bay Area conceptual legacies with young international artists; active on the fair circuit and in artist publishing.

galleries.name: Yerba Buena Center for the Arts
galleries.note: Non-collecting multidisciplinary arts centre; decades of major commissions, the Bay Area Now survey and civic-scale contemporary programming.

galleries.name: The Lab
galleries.note: Founded 1984; experimental sound, performance and installation programming in a landmark Redstone Building space, with an internationally respected commissioning record.

galleries.name: Rebecca Camacho Presents
galleries.note: Founded 2019 by a veteran of the city's leading galleries; a well-reviewed programme of emerging and mid-career artists with growing fair visibility.

galleries.name: Pier 24 Photography
galleries.note: Pilara Foundation's vast free-admission photography exhibition space, one of the largest in the world and a magnet for scholars and collectors.

galleries.name: San Francisco Camerawork
galleries.note: Founded 1974; a historic nonprofit for experimental lens-based practice, publications and emerging photographers.

galleries.name: Minnesota Street Project
galleries.note: The subsidised gallery and studio complex that reorganised the SF art map after the 49 Geary exodus; also mounts its own foundation exhibitions.

galleries.name: CULT Aimee Friberg Exhibitions
galleries.note: Curator-driven gallery known for launching Bay Area artists such as Chelsea Ryoko Wong and Rachelle Bussières into wider institutional attention.

galleries.name: Creativity Explored
galleries.note: Studio and gallery for artists with developmental disabilities since 1983; its artists now appear in museum collections and commercial galleries worldwide.

galleries.name: Gallery 16
galleries.note: Griff Williams's gallery and Urban Digital Color press; thirty years of editions and exhibitions with Rex Ray, Amy Ellingson and Chris Johanson.

galleries.name: Eleanor Harwood Gallery
galleries.note: Longstanding dealer of Bay Area emerging and mid-career artists, with an eye for craft-inflected and narrative painting.

galleries.name: Jack Fischer Gallery
galleries.note: Two decades of championing outsider, visionary and idiosyncratic contemporary work that few other SF galleries would show.

galleries.name: Chinese Culture Center of San Francisco
galleries.note: Contemporary Asian and Asian American programming through its Hilton-level galleries, 41 Ross and Edge on the Square; a leading voice in community-based contemporary art.

galleries.name: The Luggage Store Gallery
galleries.note: Since 1987 a crucible of Mission School and street-derived practice (Barry McGee, Margaret Kilgallen) plus a long-running new-music series.

galleries.name: SOMArts Cultural Center
galleries.note: Big-tent civic arts centre with curatorial residencies, the annual Día de los Muertos exhibition and decades of community-rooted contemporary shows.

galleries.name: Root Division
galleries.note: Studio-plus-gallery nonprofit linking artist residencies to arts education; a key entry point for emerging Bay Area artists.

galleries.name: Modernism Inc.
galleries.note: Martin Muller's gallery since 1979, mixing Russian avant-garde and European modernism with contemporary figures such as Mel Ramos and Gottfried Helnwein.

galleries.name: Dolby Chadwick Gallery
galleries.note: Painting-focused Union Square gallery open since 1997, with a consistent stable of contemporary figurative and abstract painters.

galleries.name: Andrea Schwartz Gallery
galleries.note: Operating since 1982; a durable SoMa space showing mid-career Bay Area painters and sculptors to corporate and private collections.

galleries.name: Brian Gross Fine Art
galleries.note: Specialist in West Coast minimalism, Light and Space and geometric abstraction; represents artists including John Zurier and Peter Alexander's circle.

galleries.name: Robert Koch Gallery
galleries.note: Long-established dealer in vintage and contemporary photography, from the Russian avant-garde to contemporary lens-based artists.

galleries.name: Euqinom Gallery
galleries.note: Monique Deschaines's photography-driven gallery, showing artists like Meghann Riepenhoff and Ian van Coller with strong fair and museum traction.

galleries.name: Nancy Toomey Fine Art
galleries.note: Abstraction-focused programme with international mid-career artists; a steady presence at Minnesota Street Project and West Coast fairs.

galleries.name: Themes+Projects
galleries.note: Curated, thematically organised exhibitions with an emphasis on photography and cross-cultural Asian–American dialogues.

galleries.name: 500 Capp Street Foundation (The David Ireland House)
galleries.note: David Ireland's conceptual house-artwork preserved as a public site with commissions and residencies by contemporary artists.

galleries.name: Recology Artist in Residence Program
galleries.note: The pioneering dump residency (since 1990) with public exhibitions of work made from discarded materials; internationally imitated.

galleries.name: SFAC Galleries
galleries.note: San Francisco Arts Commission's exhibition programme in the Veterans Building and Main Library, giving civic platform to Bay Area contemporary artists.

galleries.name: Adobe Books Backroom Gallery
galleries.note: Legendary bookstore back room where the Mission School and countless young artists showed first; still a barometer of the underground scene.

galleries.name: Slash Art
galleries.note: Nonprofit exhibition space and residency emphasising research-driven and socially engaged projects by Bay Area and international artists.

galleries.name: Gray Area
galleries.note: Art-and-technology nonprofit in the Grand Theater; festivals, immersive commissions and a leading platform for digital and new-media art.

galleries.name: Telematic Media Arts
galleries.note: Small but respected new-media nonprofit presenting experimental digital, networked and time-based work.

galleries.name: Galería de la Raza
galleries.note: Founded 1970, the historic engine of Chicano/Latinx contemporary art in the Bay Area, from Ester Hernández to today's digital mural projects.

galleries.name: Mission Cultural Center for Latino Arts
galleries.note: Community anchor since 1977 with gallery exhibitions and the Mission Gráfica print studio, a key site for Latinx contemporary practice.

galleries.name: African American Art & Culture Complex
galleries.note: Longstanding Black cultural centre presenting contemporary exhibitions, residencies and performance in the historic Fillmore.

galleries.name: Jonathan Carver Moore
galleries.note: Opened 2023 with a mission to platform BIPOC and LGBTQ+ artists; among the most watched recent additions to the SF gallery scene.

galleries.name: Serge Sorokko Gallery
galleries.note: Union Square dealer in modern and contemporary blue-chip names, from Kounellis and Botero to Chihuly and Zhang Huan.

galleries.name: Paul Thiebaud Gallery
galleries.note: Custodian of Wayne Thiebaud's legacy plus a select group of Bay Area representational painters and printmakers.

galleries.name: Caldwell Snyder Gallery
galleries.note: Since 1983, a commercially strong programme of European and American contemporary painting and sculpture with a St Helena branch.

galleries.name: Hashimoto Contemporary
galleries.note: Leading new-contemporary/illustrative gallery with New York and Los Angeles branches; large young collector base.

galleries.name: Spoke Art
galleries.note: Pop-surrealist and film-inflected gallery known for blockbuster themed shows and a national following.

galleries.name: Modern Eden Gallery
galleries.note: North Beach fixture for figurative, surrealist and craft-based contemporary work with a strong group-show tradition.

galleries.name: Voss Gallery
galleries.note: Young Mission gallery focused on emerging Bay Area painters, with an accessible, community-facing exhibition model.

galleries.name: Fouladi Projects
galleries.note: Contemporary programme spanning painting, ceramics and design-adjacent work by emerging Bay Area and international artists.

galleries.name: Hedge Gallery
galleries.note: Sculpture and collectible-design programme in Jackson Square, bridging fine art and studio furniture with museum-quality presentation.

galleries.name: Marrow Gallery
galleries.note: Neighbourhood gallery west of Twin Peaks with a serious, artist-run sensibility and a following for Bay Area abstraction and ceramics.

galleries.name: 111 Minna Gallery
galleries.note: Hybrid gallery-bar operating since 1993; an early platform for street-derived and underground SF artists.

galleries.name: Park Life
galleries.note: Design-store-with-gallery that has shown a generation of Bay Area artists and publishes small-run artist editions and books.

galleries.name: Arc Gallery
galleries.note: Artist-run gallery and studio building with juried national exhibitions and a strong local membership base.

galleries.name: Incline Gallery
galleries.note: Idiosyncratic ramped space in a former mortuary hosting emerging artists, installation and performance.

galleries.name: The Great Highway Gallery
galleries.note: Outer Sunset gallery centred on surf, landscape and photographic culture; the west side's most consistent exhibition venue.

galleries.name: Cushion Works
galleries.note: Small artist-organised space in a working upholstery shop, known for tightly curated, experimental exhibitions.

galleries.name: Ruth's Table
galleries.note: Nonprofit gallery and studio centring older adults and disability-inclusive contemporary practice, with a professionally curated programme.

galleries.name: Thacher Gallery, University of San Francisco
galleries.note: Free public university gallery with socially engaged, faith- and justice-themed contemporary exhibitions and Bay Area artist commissions.

galleries.name: Fine Arts Gallery, San Francisco State University
galleries.note: Long-running academic gallery presenting contemporary group exhibitions and Bay Area artists to a wide public audience.

galleries.name: Fort Mason Center for Arts & Culture (Gallery 308)
galleries.note: Waterfront arts campus whose Gallery 308 and Festival Pavilion host large-scale contemporary exhibitions and commissions.

galleries.name: The Midway
galleries.note: Warehouse arts complex with a gallery and residency programme bridging music, immersive installation and visual art.

galleries.name: Weinstein Gallery
galleries.note: Large downtown operation dealing in surrealism and modern masters alongside contemporary figuration; a high-traffic commercial presence.

galleries.name: Hackett Mill
galleries.note: Private dealership and exhibition space handling postwar California artists and estates, with strong secondary-market scholarship.

galleries.name: Creative Growth Art Center
galleries.note: The world's pioneering studio and gallery for artists with disabilities (since 1974); its artists are in MoMA, SFMOMA and the Pompidou.

galleries.name: Kala Art Institute
galleries.note: Printmaking and media residency centre with an active gallery; a four-decade fixture of Bay Area artist development.

galleries.name: Paulson Fontaine Press
galleries.note: Fine-art print publisher and gallery producing editions with Martin Puryear, Kerry James Marshall and the Gee's Bend quilters.

galleries.name: Traywick Contemporary
galleries.note: Long-running East Bay gallery with a conceptually grounded roster and consistent art-fair participation.

galleries.name: pt.2 Gallery
galleries.note: One of the East Bay's most visible young galleries, showing emerging painters with national fair presence.

galleries.name: Johansson Projects
galleries.note: Uptown Oakland gallery known for material-driven, offbeat contemporary work since 2006.

galleries.name: Interface Gallery
galleries.note: Tiny curator-run nonprofit with an outsized critical reputation for focused, experimental solo projects.

galleries.name: Pro Arts
galleries.note: Since 1974 the East Bay's main artist-service nonprofit, running the Open Studios and a commons-model exhibition programme.

galleries.name: Berkeley Art Center
galleries.note: Live Oak Park nonprofit presenting contemporary Bay Area exhibitions and public programmes for more than fifty years.

galleries.name: NIAD Art Center
galleries.note: Progressive studio and gallery for disabled artists whose programme has gained major curatorial attention nationally.

galleries.name: Mercury 20 Gallery
galleries.note: Artist-run cooperative gallery, a durable node of Oakland's Art Murmur ecosystem.

galleries.name: Transmission Gallery
galleries.note: Small West Oakland gallery with a steady programme of Bay Area painting, sculpture and works on paper.

galleries.name: The Compound Gallery
galleries.note: Gallery, studios and an art-subscription programme that has broadened access to collecting emerging Bay Area artists.
